comment: Seaways and river gorges narrower than the continental pass's 10 km lattice, which the pass burns into its node elevations where the terrain is today's (rivers Task 8b round 2; gorges Task 11). A strait (the default kind) lowers its polyline's nodes to its sill depth; a gorge lowers them to its river's surface, given per point as [lat, lon, level_m] and interpolated between points. Either level moves with the era's own shift from the present-day overview, so an era whose sea stood below a strait's sill keeps the basin closed. Read by timefly_core::hydrology::straits and by tools/bake/timefly_bake/hydro_ref.py.

straits.name: Bosporus
straits.source: Bosporus centreline from the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea. Sill: Gregg, M.C. & Ozsoy, E. (2002), Flow, water mass changes, and hydraulics in the Bosphorus, J. Geophys. Res. 107(C3), 3016, doi:10.1029/2000JC000485, para. 52: 'Most of South Sill is 30-40 m deep, but a central ridge rises to 28 m'; -35 m is the middle of that range.
straits.note: The strait is 0.7-3.5 km wide and about 31 km long: below the 5' overview and the lattice, so without it the Black Sea is an inland basin that merges with the Caspian through the Manych.

straits.name: Danube Bend
straits.source: The Danube's gorge through the volcanic hills at Visegrad, from Esztergom to Budapest: Karatson, D. (2015), Danube Bend: Miocene Half-Caldera and Pleistocene Gorge, in Loczy, D. (ed.), Landscapes and Landforms of Hungary, Springer, pp. 129-137, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-08997-3_16. Course and levels: the lowest ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cell within 2' of each point (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74), 105 m at Esztergom falling to 101.5 m at Budapest.
straits.note: Without it the 10 km lattice closes the Bend, and the Danube leaves the Little Hungarian Plain past Lake Balaton and down the Sio, missing Budapest (rivers Task 11 reality check).

straits.name: Iron Gate
straits.source: The Danube's Iron Gates gorges from Golubac to the Sip gorge below the Iron Gate I dam (dam at 44.671 N, 22.530 E; a 134 km route of gorges 150-230 m wide at their narrowest): Wikipedia, 'Iron Gates' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Gates, read 2026-11-26). Course and levels: the lowest ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cell within 2' of each point (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74): the Iron Gate I reservoir's surface, 66-68 m, down to Orsova, and the river below the dam at about 41 m.
straits.note: Narrower than ETOPO's 60 arc-second cells as well as the lattice: the 10 km lattice and the 1' data both close it above 100 m, so without it the Pannonian basin spills north through the Moravian Gate (about 300 m) and the Danube reaches the Baltic by the Oder (rivers Task 8b, Task 11 reality check).

straits.name: Upper Indus
straits.source: The Indus from the south-west edge of Tibet through the Ladakh and Zanskar ranges to its Zanskar confluence near Nimo, a reach of gorges (about 7 m/km from Mahe to Upshi): Kumar, A. & Srivastava, P. (2017), The role of climate and tectonics in aggradation and incision of the Indus River in the Ladakh Himalaya during the late Quaternary, Quaternary Research 87(3), 363-385, doi:10.1017/qua.2017.19. Course and levels: the river traced by the 1' reference pass over ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74; tools/bake/timefly_bake/hydro_ref.py, the indus box), simplified to 1 km, levels its running minimum downstream.
straits.note: Without it the 10 km lattice closes the valley in Ladakh, and the Indus's headwaters spill east through Tibet's lake basins to the Bay of Bengal (rivers Task 11 reality check).
